In 1973, Willie Colón stopped touring to focus on record production and other business enterprises. Lavoe was given the opportunity to become the bandleader of his own orchestra.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-salsa_centro-8) He and his band traveled the world on their own, and he would also be a guest singer with the [Fania All-Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars "Fania All-Stars") for several shows. One of the group's notable performances took place in the [Kinshasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kinshasa "Kinshasa") province of [Zaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire "Zaire") (modern-day Democratic Republic of Congo), where the group performed at the [Zaire 74](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire_74 "Zaire 74") music festival as part of the activities promoting [the Rumble in the Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Rumble_in_the_Jungle "The Rumble in the Jungle"), a boxing fight between [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali") and [George Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Foreman "George Foreman") for the heavyweight championship of the [World Boxing Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Council "World Boxing Council") and [World Boxing Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Boxing_Association "World Boxing Association").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Salsa_Connects-21)

The [Fania All-Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars "Fania All-Stars") recorded several of its tracks during live concerts. Lavoe was part of the group when the All-Stars returned to [Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium_(1923) "Yankee Stadium (1923)") in 1975, where the band recorded a two volume production titled _[Live at Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1970s\_in\_Latin\_music "1970s in Latin music")_. The event featured the top vocalists of [Fania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") and Vaya Records. Lavoe was included in the group along with [Ismael Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Miranda "Ismael Miranda"), [Cheo Feliciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheo_Feliciano "Cheo Feliciano"), [Justo Betancourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justo_Betancourt "Justo Betancourt"), [Ismael Quintana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Quintana "Ismael Quintana"), [Bobby Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cruz "Bobby Cruz"), [Pete "El Conde" Rodriguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_%22El_Conde%22_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pete \"El Conde\" Rodríguez"), [Santos Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Col%C3%B3n "Santos Colón"), and [Celia Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celia_Cruz "Celia Cruz"). Lavoe recorded songs with the band in fifteen different productions, serving as vocalist on twenty-three songs. Besides recording songs with the band, Lavoe was also present in three movies filmed and produced by [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records"); these were: _[Our Latin Thing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our\_Latin\_Thing "Our Latin Thing")_, _Salsa_, and _Celia Cruz with the Fania All Stars: Live in Africa_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-salsa_centro-8) His Colón-produced albums would be best sellers; cuts from these albums were hits in Puerto Rico and the rest of Latin America:

*   Lavoe's recording of [Tite Curet Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tite_Curet_Alonso "Tite Curet Alonso")'s "Periódico de Ayer" was a number-one hit on Mexican charts for four straight months. It was also a strong hit in several Caribbean countries and South America.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Bac%C3%A1n-12)
*   As a producer, Willie Colón had Lavoe record what would become his [signature song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Signature_song "Signature song"), the [Ruben Blades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruben_Blades "Ruben Blades")-authored song "El Cantante" against Blades's protests (Blades wanted to record the song on his own). Blades has repeatedly acknowledged since then that Lavoe raised his song to classic status[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-22) and that Lavoe's performance was much better than what he would accomplish with it.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
*   In 1975, on his _[La Voz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La\_Voz\_(album) "La Voz (album)")_ Album, Lavoe did a cover of [Chappottin Y Sus Estrellas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chappottin_Y_Sus_Estrellas "Chappottin Y Sus Estrellas") 1957 song “Rompe Saragüey”,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-23) which became a major success.
*   The Lavoe song "Bandolera" was a strong seller in Puerto Rico, despite vigorous protests from Puerto Rican feminists about its lyrics and soneos - Lavoe twice offers the song's subject a beating.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Bac%C3%A1n-12)
*   Lavoe's recording of the classic Cuban song by [Eliseo Grenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliseo_Grenet "Eliseo Grenet")[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-24) based on Cuban poet [Nicolás Guillén](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicol%C3%A1s_Guill%C3%A9n "Nicolás Guillén")'s poem "Sóngoro Cosongo", set to salsa music, was another major hit.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-American_Salsa-17)
*   The controversial [jíbaro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J%C3%ADbaro_music "Jíbaro music") song "Joven Contra Viejo" featured Lavoe and [Daniel Santos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Santos_(singer) "Daniel Santos (singer)") settling their age-based differences on stage not without a heavy dose of humor and, yet again, [Yomo Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yomo_Toro "Yomo Toro")'s cuatro music as a backdrop. Another major Christmas hit on _[Billboard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard\_charts "Billboard charts")_ top hits in the tropical genre in 1979 includes a song from singer/composer [Miguel Poventud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Poventud "Miguel Poventud") "Una Pena En La Navidad" from the same album titled _[Feliz Navidad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feliz\_Navidad\_(H%C3%A9ctor\_Lavoe\_album) "Feliz Navidad (Héctor Lavoe album)")_.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Bac%C3%A1n-12)
*   Lavoe's final hit, "El Rey de la Puntualidad" (The King of Punctuality), is a humorous takeoff on Lavoe's constant tardiness and occasional absenteeism from shows.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Babalao-26) Lavoe followed the Santeria priest's advice and cut all communication with his family and friends for a period of two months.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Babalao-26) Following this recording, Héctor reappeared confident and apparently free of his drug addiction.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Babalao-26)

## Last years and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Last years and death")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2c/Tumba_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe%2C_Cementerio_Civil_de_Ponce%2C_Bo._Portugu%C3%A9s_Urbano%2C_Ponce%2C_Puerto_Rico%2C_mirando_al_oeste_%28DSC01432A%29.jpg/330px-Tumba_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe%2C_Cementerio_Civil_de_Ponce%2C_Bo._Portugu%C3%A9s_Urbano%2C_Ponce%2C_Puerto_Rico%2C_mirando_al_oeste_%28DSC01432A%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tumba_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe,_Cementerio_Civil_de_Ponce,_Bo._Portugu%C3%A9s_Urbano,_Ponce,_Puerto_Rico,_mirando_al_oeste_(DSC01432A).jpg)

Lavoe's grave at [Cementerio Civil de Ponce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cementerio_Civil_de_Ponce "Cementerio Civil de Ponce"), Bo. [Portugués Urbano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portugu%C3%A9s_Urbano "Portugués Urbano"), Ponce.

Following his rehabilitation, Lavoe's life was plagued by tragic events, emotional turmoil, and pain.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Babalao-26) In 1987, his seventeen-year-old son Héctor Jr. was accidentally shot and killed by a friend. In the same period, his apartment in [Rego Park, Queens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rego_Park,_Queens "Rego Park, Queens"), was destroyed in a fire.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-27) One year later, Héctor was scheduled to perform at the [Rubén Rodríguez Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Rodr%C3%ADguez_Coliseum "Rubén Rodríguez Coliseum") in [Bayamón, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bayam%C3%B3n,_Puerto_Rico "Bayamón, Puerto Rico"), on the night of Saturday, June 25, 1988. Sales for the concert were poor, and promoter Rick Sostre decided to cancel the concert two hours before concert time. Héctor, defiant to the end, and knowing that it would be one of the last times he would perform in Puerto Rico, decided, against the promoter's wishes, to perform for the public, who had paid to see the concert.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Triump-3) The next day, Sunday, June 26, 1988, Héctor attempted suicide by jumping off the ninth floor of the [Regency Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyatt_Regency "Hyatt Regency")[Condado](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condado_(Santurce) "Condado (Santurce)") in [San Juan, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Puerto_Rico "San Juan, Puerto Rico").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-tbxmix-16) He survived the attempt, but from that day forward, would never completely recover.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Triump-3)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-NPR_2007-28)

On September 2, 1990, Héctor gave his last large, public performance with the Fania All Stars at the [Meadowlands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meadowlands_Arena "Meadowlands Arena") in New Jersey.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-His_Life-15) It was meant to be his comeback concert, but Héctor could only sing a few notes of his famous song "Mi Gente".[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-His_Life-15) It is believed his final public performance was a brief appearance at the club S.O.B.'s in New York City, in April 1992.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-29)

On June 29, 1993, Héctor died at [Saint Clare's Hospital (Manhattan)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Clare's_Hospital_(Manhattan) "Saint Clare's Hospital (Manhattan)") from a complication from AIDS.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-salsa_centro-8) He was 46. He was initially buried in [Saint Raymond's Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Raymond's_Cemetery_(Bronx) "Saint Raymond's Cemetery (Bronx)") in [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx"). In June 2002, the remains of Lavoe and his son were exhumed at his family's request and reburied in his native [Ponce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ponce,_Puerto_Rico "Ponce, Puerto Rico"), along with his widow Nilda who had died a few weeks before. His remains are at the [Cementerio Civil de Ponce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cementerio_Civil_de_Ponce "Cementerio Civil de Ponce") (Ponce Civil Cemetery), in the city's [Portugués Urbano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barrio_Portugu%C3%A9s_Urbano "Barrio Portugués Urbano") neighborhood.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-30)

## Recognition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Recognition")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/88/Estatua_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe_en_Tablado_La_Guancha%2C_Barrio_Playa%2C_Ponce%2C_PR_%28DSC01187%29.jpg/250px-Estatua_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe_en_Tablado_La_Guancha%2C_Barrio_Playa%2C_Ponce%2C_PR_%28DSC01187%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Estatua_de_H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe_en_Tablado_La_Guancha,_Barrio_Playa,_Ponce,_PR_(DSC01187).jpg)

[Lavoe's statue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe_(statue) "Héctor Lavoe (statue)") in [Paseo Tablado La Guancha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paseo_Tablado_La_Guancha "Paseo Tablado La Guancha"), Ponce, Puerto Rico.

Lavoe's life has inspired two [biographical films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biographical_film "Biographical film"). The first, _[El Cantante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El\_Cantante "El Cantante")_, was produced by salsa artist [Marc Anthony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Anthony "Marc Anthony"), who played Lavoe, and [Jennifer Lopez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Lopez "Jennifer Lopez") as Hector's wife, Nilda (known as "Puchi" by close friends).[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-31) Salsa singer [La India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_India "La India") also began production of her own [biopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopic "Biopic") of Lavoe's life, titled _The Singer_, with actor and singer [Raulito Carbonell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raulito_Carbonell "Raulito Carbonell") in the lead role.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-32) Production was suspended in August 2008 after the director, Anthony Felton, reported that it was over budget. Carbonell noted that he would reconsider his involvement if production were to resume.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Carbonell-33) The movie was eventually completed, in 2011, as "Lavoe: The Untold Story".[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-34)

An [Off-Broadway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Off-Broadway "Off-Broadway") production based on Lavoe's life titled _¿Quién mató a Héctor Lavoe?_ (_Who Killed Hector Lavoe?_) was a success in the late 1990s.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-35) It starred singer [Domingo Quiñones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Domingo_Qui%C3%B1ones "Domingo Quiñones") in the lead role.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-36) Carbonell's decision to distance himself from the film directed by Felton was the direct result of his involvement in a tour of _Quien Mato a Héctor Lavoe?_ in Puerto Rico, and, depending upon negotiations, possibly [Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peru "Peru") and [Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colombia "Colombia").[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-Carbonell-33)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-37) An urban tribute album was released in late 2007 performed by several reggaeton artists such as [Don Omar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Omar "Don Omar") which sampled Lavoe's voice.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-38)

In Ponce, he is recognized at the [Park for the Illustrious Ponce Citizens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricentennial_Park_(Ponce,_Puerto_Rico) "Tricentennial Park (Ponce, Puerto Rico)").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-39) Lavoe was posthumously inducted into the [International Latin Music Hall of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_Latin_Music_Hall_of_Fame "International Latin Music Hall of Fame") in 2000.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-40)

[La Guancha Recreational and Cultural Complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Guancha_Recreational_and_Cultural_Complex "La Guancha Recreational and Cultural Complex") in his hometown of Ponce, Puerto Rico, [honored Hector with a statue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe_(statue) "Héctor Lavoe (statue)"). The $60,000 statue is 2 meters (6 1/2 feet) tall, weighs 1 ton and portrays Lavoe with a microphone in his right hand and a pair of [maracas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maraca "Maraca") in his left.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-41)

[Tremont Avenue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tremont_Avenue "Tremont Avenue") in the New York City's Bronx borough was renamed in his honor and remembrance.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-NYCStreetnames-2009-42)

In 2023, _[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling\_Stone "Rolling Stone")_ ranked Lavoe at number 73 on its list of the 200 Greatest Singers of All Time.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/H%C3%A9ctor_Lavoe#cite_note-43)

The **Fania All Stars** is a musical group formed in 1968 as a showcase for the musicians on [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records"), the leading [salsa music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salsa_music "Salsa music") record label of the time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Beginnings")]

In 1964, [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") was founded in New York City by [Jerry Masucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Masucci "Jerry Masucci"), an Italian-American lawyer with a love for [Cuban music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Cuba "Music of Cuba"), and [Johnny Pacheco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Pacheco "Johnny Pacheco"), a flutist, [percussionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussion_instrument "Percussion instrument") and [bandleader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandleader "Bandleader") born in the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic "Dominican Republic") but raised in the [South Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bronx "South Bronx") who had similar musical tastes.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-:0-2) Masucci later bought out his partner Pacheco from Fania Entertainment Group, Ltd. and was the sole owner until his death in December 1997.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-3)

Throughout the early years, [Fania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") used to distribute its records around New York. Eventually success from Pacheco's _Cañonazo_ recording would lead the label to develop its roster. Masucci and Pacheco, now executive negotiator and musical director respectively, began acquiring musicians such as [Bobby Valentín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Valent%C3%ADn "Bobby Valentín"), [Larry Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Harlow_(musician) "Larry Harlow (musician)"), and [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto").

### Success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Success")]

In 1968, [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") created a continuously revolving line-up of entertainers known as the Fania All-Stars. They were considered some of the best Latin Music performers in the world at that time. The original lineup consisted of:

*   Band Leaders: [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto"), [Joe Bataan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Bataan "Joe Bataan"), Willie Colon, [Larry Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Harlow_(musician) "Larry Harlow (musician)"), [Monguito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monguito "Monguito"), [Johnny Pacheco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Pacheco "Johnny Pacheco"), [Louie Ramirez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louie_Ramirez "Louie Ramirez"), Ralph Robles, [Mongo Santamaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongo_Santamar%C3%ADa "Mongo Santamaría"), and [Bobby Valentin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Valentin "Bobby Valentin").
*   Singers; Héctor Lavoe, [Adalberto Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalberto_Santiago "Adalberto Santiago"), [Pete "El Conde" Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_%22El_Conde%22_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pete \"El Conde\" Rodríguez"), and [Ismael Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Miranda "Ismael Miranda").
*   Other Musicians; [La La](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_%22LaLa%22_Brooks "Dolores \"LaLa\" Brooks"), Ray Maldonado, Ralph Marzan, [Orestes Vilató](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orestes_Vilat%C3%B3 "Orestes Vilató"), Roberto Rodriguez, Jose Rodriguez, and [Barry Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Rogers "Barry Rogers").
*   Special Guests; [Tito Puente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Puente "Tito Puente"), [Eddie Palmieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Palmieri "Eddie Palmieri"), [Ricardo Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Ray "Ricardo Ray") and [Jimmy Sabater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Sabater "Jimmy Sabater").

They recorded _Live at the Red Garter, Volumes 1 and 2_ with this original lineup. On August 26, 1971, they recorded _Live at the Cheetah, Volumes 1 and 2._[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-4) It exhibited the entire All-Star family performing before a capacity audience in New York City's Cheetah Lounge.

Following sell-out concerts in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), and [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama "Panama"), the All-Stars embarked on their first appearance at [New York's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")[Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium") on August 24, 1973.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-5) The All-Stars performed before more than 40,000 spectators in a concert that featured [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto"), Willie Colón, Edwin Tito Asencio, [Rubén Blades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Blades "Rubén Blades"), Larry Harlow, Johnny Pacheco, [Roberto Roena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Roena "Roberto Roena"), [Pellín Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pell%C3%ADn_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pellín Rodríguez"), Bobby Valentín, and [Jorge Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Santana "Jorge Santana") (younger brother of [Carlos Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Santana "Carlos Santana")), [Celia Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celia_Cruz "Celia Cruz"), Héctor Lavoe, [Cheo Feliciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheo_Feliciano "Cheo Feliciano"), [Ismael Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Miranda "Ismael Miranda"), [Justo Betancourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justo_Betancourt "Justo Betancourt"), [Ismael Quintana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Quintana "Ismael Quintana"), [Pete "El Conde" Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_%22El_Conde%22_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pete \"El Conde\" Rodríguez"), [Bobby Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cruz "Bobby Cruz") and [Santos Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Col%C3%B3n "Santos Colón"). _Live at Yankee Stadium_ was included in the second set of 50 recordings in the U.S. [National Recording Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recording_Registry "National Recording Registry"), solidifying the All-Stars as "culturally, historically, and aesthetically significant."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-6)

In 1974, the All-Stars performed in [Zaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire "Zaire"), Africa, at the 80,000-seat [Stade du 20 mai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Tata_Rapha%C3%ABl "Stade Tata Raphaël") in Kinshasa. This was captured on film and released as _Live in Africa_ (_Salsa Madness_ in the UK). This Zairean appearance occurred along with [James Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown "James Brown") and others at a music festival held in conjunction with the [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali")/[George Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Foreman "George Foreman")[heavyweight title fight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumble_in_the_Jungle "Rumble in the Jungle").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-:0-2) Footage of the performance was included in the 2008 documentary _[Soul Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Power\_(film) "Soul Power (film)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-7)

To attain a wider market for salsa music, Fania made a deal with [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records") in the US for a series of crossover albums by the All-Stars, beginning with _Delicate and Jumpy_ (1976), in which [Steve Winwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Winwood "Steve Winwood") united with the All-Stars' Pacheco, Valentin, Barreto, and Roena. During the same year, the Fania All-Stars made their sole UK appearance, at [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")'s [Lyceum Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyceum_Theatre,_London "Lyceum Theatre, London"), with Winwood appearing as guest.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-8)

In 1978 the All-Stars released _Live_, recorded in concert on July 11, 1975, at San Juan's [Roberto Clemente Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente_Coliseum "Roberto Clemente Coliseum"). In 1979, they travelled to [Havana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana "Havana"), Cuba, to participate in the [Havana Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana_Jam "Havana Jam") festival that took place between March 2–4, alongside [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Stephen Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Stills "Stephen Stills"), the CBS Jazz All-Stars, [Trio of Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trio_of_Doom "Trio of Doom"), [Billy Swan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Swan "Billy Swan"), [Bonnie Bramlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Bramlett "Bonnie Bramlett"), [Weather Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_Report "Weather Report"), and [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel"), plus Cuban artists such as [Irakere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irakere "Irakere"), [Pacho Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacho_Alonso "Pacho Alonso"), [Tata Güines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_G%C3%BCines "Tata Güines"), and [Orquesta Aragón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orquesta_Arag%C3%B3n "Orquesta Aragón"). Their performance is captured on Ernesto Juan Castellanos's documentary _Havana Jam '79_. During the same year the All-Stars released _Crossover_ on Columbia and _Habana Jam_ on Fania, which came from a concert recorded in Havana on March 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-9)

### Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 2009, a historical documentary, _Latin Music USA_, shown on [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service "Public Broadcasting Service") TV, featured an episode on the Fania All-Stars, their evolution, career, and later demise.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-10) In 2009 as well, the All-Stars returned to the stage, opening [Carlos Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Santana "Carlos Santana")'s world tour in [Bogotá, Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá"). The presentation caused mixed feelings inside the salsa circle though, mainly because they were treated as seconds by the concert's organizers.

In March 2011, and subsequently in November 2012, a limited roster of the All-Stars performed in [Lima, Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-12) One thing to note about the 2012 performance is the return of [Ruben Blades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Blades "Rubén Blades"). Ismael Quintana was not present in the November 2012 performance though, as well as [Yomo Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yomo_Toro "Yomo Toro") (Yomo died on June 30, 2012). In October 2013, a new, complete roster of the All-Stars performed in [San Juan, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Puerto_Rico "San Juan, Puerto Rico"), celebrating the 40th anniversary of their first performance in San Juan. This roster included the return of [Orestes Vilato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orestes_Vilat%C3%B3 "Orestes Vilató") and Luigi Texidor, as well as the participation of [Andy Montañez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Monta%C3%B1ez "Andy Montañez"), Cita Rodriguez (Pete's daughter) and Willie Colón. This was Cheo Feliciano's last performance with the All-Stars before dying in a car accident in April 2014 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-13) In 2015 the Fania All-Stars were chosen to receive [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s honorary [Latin Heritage Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP_Latin_Heritage_Award "ASCAP Latin Heritage Award").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-14) The All-Stars were set to perform in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), New York City on August 24 as part of the closing ceremony of the 50th anniversary celebration of the legendary Fania Records label.

In 2019, many of the classic Fania albums were re-issued by Concord/Craft Recordings on vinyl as part of the renewed interest in the vinyl record format.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-15)

The **Fania All Stars** is a musical group formed in 1968 as a showcase for the musicians on [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records"), the leading [salsa music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salsa_music "Salsa music") record label of the time.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-1)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Beginnings")]

In 1964, [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") was founded in New York City by [Jerry Masucci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Masucci "Jerry Masucci"), an Italian-American lawyer with a love for [Cuban music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Cuba "Music of Cuba"), and [Johnny Pacheco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Pacheco "Johnny Pacheco"), a flutist, [percussionist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percussion_instrument "Percussion instrument") and [bandleader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandleader "Bandleader") born in the [Dominican Republic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominican_Republic "Dominican Republic") but raised in the [South Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Bronx "South Bronx") who had similar musical tastes.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-:0-2) Masucci later bought out his partner Pacheco from Fania Entertainment Group, Ltd. and was the sole owner until his death in December 1997.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-3)

Throughout the early years, [Fania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") used to distribute its records around New York. Eventually success from Pacheco's _Cañonazo_ recording would lead the label to develop its roster. Masucci and Pacheco, now executive negotiator and musical director respectively, began acquiring musicians such as [Bobby Valentín](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Valent%C3%ADn "Bobby Valentín"), [Larry Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Harlow_(musician) "Larry Harlow (musician)"), and [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto").

### Success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Success")]

In 1968, [Fania Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_Records "Fania Records") created a continuously revolving line-up of entertainers known as the Fania All-Stars. They were considered some of the best Latin Music performers in the world at that time. The original lineup consisted of:

*   Band Leaders: [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto"), [Joe Bataan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Bataan "Joe Bataan"), Willie Colon, [Larry Harlow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_Harlow_(musician) "Larry Harlow (musician)"), [Monguito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monguito "Monguito"), [Johnny Pacheco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johnny_Pacheco "Johnny Pacheco"), [Louie Ramirez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louie_Ramirez "Louie Ramirez"), Ralph Robles, [Mongo Santamaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mongo_Santamar%C3%ADa "Mongo Santamaría"), and [Bobby Valentin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Valentin "Bobby Valentin").
*   Singers; Héctor Lavoe, [Adalberto Santiago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adalberto_Santiago "Adalberto Santiago"), [Pete "El Conde" Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_%22El_Conde%22_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pete \"El Conde\" Rodríguez"), and [Ismael Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Miranda "Ismael Miranda").
*   Other Musicians; [La La](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolores_%22LaLa%22_Brooks "Dolores \"LaLa\" Brooks"), Ray Maldonado, Ralph Marzan, [Orestes Vilató](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orestes_Vilat%C3%B3 "Orestes Vilató"), Roberto Rodriguez, Jose Rodriguez, and [Barry Rogers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry_Rogers "Barry Rogers").
*   Special Guests; [Tito Puente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tito_Puente "Tito Puente"), [Eddie Palmieri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddie_Palmieri "Eddie Palmieri"), [Ricardo Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricardo_Ray "Ricardo Ray") and [Jimmy Sabater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jimmy_Sabater "Jimmy Sabater").

They recorded _Live at the Red Garter, Volumes 1 and 2_ with this original lineup. On August 26, 1971, they recorded _Live at the Cheetah, Volumes 1 and 2._[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-4) It exhibited the entire All-Star family performing before a capacity audience in New York City's Cheetah Lounge.

Following sell-out concerts in [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago"), and [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama "Panama"), the All-Stars embarked on their first appearance at [New York's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City "New York City")[Yankee Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yankee_Stadium "Yankee Stadium") on August 24, 1973.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-5) The All-Stars performed before more than 40,000 spectators in a concert that featured [Ray Barretto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Barretto "Ray Barretto"), Willie Colón, Edwin Tito Asencio, [Rubén Blades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Blades "Rubén Blades"), Larry Harlow, Johnny Pacheco, [Roberto Roena](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Roena "Roberto Roena"), [Pellín Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pell%C3%ADn_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pellín Rodríguez"), Bobby Valentín, and [Jorge Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jorge_Santana "Jorge Santana") (younger brother of [Carlos Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Santana "Carlos Santana")), [Celia Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Celia_Cruz "Celia Cruz"), Héctor Lavoe, [Cheo Feliciano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheo_Feliciano "Cheo Feliciano"), [Ismael Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Miranda "Ismael Miranda"), [Justo Betancourt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justo_Betancourt "Justo Betancourt"), [Ismael Quintana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ismael_Quintana "Ismael Quintana"), [Pete "El Conde" Rodríguez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_%22El_Conde%22_Rodr%C3%ADguez "Pete \"El Conde\" Rodríguez"), [Bobby Cruz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Cruz "Bobby Cruz") and [Santos Colón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santos_Col%C3%B3n "Santos Colón"). _Live at Yankee Stadium_ was included in the second set of 50 recordings in the U.S. [National Recording Registry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Recording_Registry "National Recording Registry"), solidifying the All-Stars as "culturally, historically, and aesthetically significant."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-6)

In 1974, the All-Stars performed in [Zaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zaire "Zaire"), Africa, at the 80,000-seat [Stade du 20 mai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stade_Tata_Rapha%C3%ABl "Stade Tata Raphaël") in Kinshasa. This was captured on film and released as _Live in Africa_ (_Salsa Madness_ in the UK). This Zairean appearance occurred along with [James Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Brown "James Brown") and others at a music festival held in conjunction with the [Muhammad Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muhammad_Ali "Muhammad Ali")/[George Foreman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Foreman "George Foreman")[heavyweight title fight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumble_in_the_Jungle "Rumble in the Jungle").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-:0-2) Footage of the performance was included in the 2008 documentary _[Soul Power](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soul\_Power\_(film) "Soul Power (film)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-7)

To attain a wider market for salsa music, Fania made a deal with [Columbia Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Records "Columbia Records") in the US for a series of crossover albums by the All-Stars, beginning with _Delicate and Jumpy_ (1976), in which [Steve Winwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Winwood "Steve Winwood") united with the All-Stars' Pacheco, Valentin, Barreto, and Roena. During the same year, the Fania All-Stars made their sole UK appearance, at [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London")'s [Lyceum Ballroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyceum_Theatre,_London "Lyceum Theatre, London"), with Winwood appearing as guest.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-8)

In 1978 the All-Stars released _Live_, recorded in concert on July 11, 1975, at San Juan's [Roberto Clemente Coliseum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roberto_Clemente_Coliseum "Roberto Clemente Coliseum"). In 1979, they travelled to [Havana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana "Havana"), Cuba, to participate in the [Havana Jam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Havana_Jam "Havana Jam") festival that took place between March 2–4, alongside [Rita Coolidge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rita_Coolidge "Rita Coolidge"), [Kris Kristofferson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kris_Kristofferson "Kris Kristofferson"), [Stephen Stills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Stills "Stephen Stills"), the CBS Jazz All-Stars, [Trio of Doom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trio_of_Doom "Trio of Doom"), [Billy Swan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Swan "Billy Swan"), [Bonnie Bramlett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonnie_Bramlett "Bonnie Bramlett"), [Weather Report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weather_Report "Weather Report"), and [Billy Joel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billy_Joel "Billy Joel"), plus Cuban artists such as [Irakere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irakere "Irakere"), [Pacho Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacho_Alonso "Pacho Alonso"), [Tata Güines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tata_G%C3%BCines "Tata Güines"), and [Orquesta Aragón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orquesta_Arag%C3%B3n "Orquesta Aragón"). Their performance is captured on Ernesto Juan Castellanos's documentary _Havana Jam '79_. During the same year the All-Stars released _Crossover_ on Columbia and _Habana Jam_ on Fania, which came from a concert recorded in Havana on March 2.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-9)

### Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fania_All-Stars&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Legacy")]

In 2009, a historical documentary, _Latin Music USA_, shown on [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service "Public Broadcasting Service") TV, featured an episode on the Fania All-Stars, their evolution, career, and later demise.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-10) In 2009 as well, the All-Stars returned to the stage, opening [Carlos Santana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Santana "Carlos Santana")'s world tour in [Bogotá, Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bogot%C3%A1 "Bogotá"). The presentation caused mixed feelings inside the salsa circle though, mainly because they were treated as seconds by the concert's organizers.

In March 2011, and subsequently in November 2012, a limited roster of the All-Stars performed in [Lima, Peru](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lima "Lima").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-12) One thing to note about the 2012 performance is the return of [Ruben Blades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rub%C3%A9n_Blades "Rubén Blades"). Ismael Quintana was not present in the November 2012 performance though, as well as [Yomo Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yomo_Toro "Yomo Toro") (Yomo died on June 30, 2012). In October 2013, a new, complete roster of the All-Stars performed in [San Juan, Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Juan,_Puerto_Rico "San Juan, Puerto Rico"), celebrating the 40th anniversary of their first performance in San Juan. This roster included the return of [Orestes Vilato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orestes_Vilat%C3%B3 "Orestes Vilató") and Luigi Texidor, as well as the participation of [Andy Montañez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Monta%C3%B1ez "Andy Montañez"), Cita Rodriguez (Pete's daughter) and Willie Colón. This was Cheo Feliciano's last performance with the All-Stars before dying in a car accident in April 2014 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-13) In 2015 the Fania All-Stars were chosen to receive [ASCAP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP "ASCAP")'s honorary [Latin Heritage Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ASCAP_Latin_Heritage_Award "ASCAP Latin Heritage Award").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-14) The All-Stars were set to perform in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park"), New York City on August 24 as part of the closing ceremony of the 50th anniversary celebration of the legendary Fania Records label.

In 2019, many of the classic Fania albums were re-issued by Concord/Craft Recordings on vinyl as part of the renewed interest in the vinyl record format.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fania_All-Stars#cite_note-15)
